sec: ADPKD (contd): nephrectomy indications, brain note & ARPKD · p789

items.q: Match the remaining extrarenal associations of ADPKD — 1) Cardiac valve  2) Aorta  3) Abdominal wall … A) Aortic root dilatation  B) Mitral valve prolapse  C) Inguinal hernia
items.exp: Extrarenal associations continued: mitral valve prolapse (d), AR/aortic root dilatation (e), and abdominal wall/inguinal hernia (f). (Book p789)

items.q: Which of the following is the correct indication for pre-transplant nephrectomy in ADPKD?
opts: Uncontrolled hypertension, infection, obstruction and bleeding
A single previous episode of cyst haemorrhage
items.exp: Indications for pre-transplant nephrectomy: (a) infection, (b) obstruction (no space for the transplanted kidney), (c) bleeding, (d) uncontrolled hypertension. (Book p789)

items.q: A patient with ADPKD and massively enlarged kidneys is being prepared for transplantation. Nephrectomy is indicated for the specific reason that:
opts: There is no space for the transplanted kidney (obstruction)
The kidneys contain more than 5% nephrons involved
Pre-transplant nephrectomy is mandatory in all ADPKD
Liver cysts will not be reversed otherwise
items.exp: Pre-transplant nephrectomy indications include obstruction — no space for the transplanted kidney — along with infection, bleeding and uncontrolled hypertension. (Book p789)

items.q: In ADPKD the brain has no cysts.
opts: False — brain cysts are the hallmark of ADPKD
False — brain cysts occur in 10% of patients
items.exp: Note: brain has no cysts in ADPKD, although saccular aneurysms of the anterior circulation (Berry aneurysms) can occur. (Book p789)

opts: Autosomal recessive and can be diagnosed in utero as small cysts in the medulla
Autosomal dominant and usually presents in middle age
X-linked and presents with haematuria in boys
Acquired and seen in adults with recurrent stones
items.exp: ARPKD: autosomal recessive, and it can be diagnosed in utero (small cysts in the medulla). (Book p789)

items.q: Fill up: In ARPKD the gene defect is on chromosome 6: ______, which forms the fibrocystin–polyductin complex.
items.exp: ARPKD gene defect: on chromosome 6 — PKHD1 → fibrocystin–polyductin complex, whose defect affects the cilia/centrosome complex. (Book p789)

items.q: Complete the ARPKD flowchart showing which ducts are affected and the resulting lesions — 1) Collecting duct  2) Biliary duct … A) Congenital hepatic fibrosis/Caroli's syndrome/biliary ectasia  B) Medullary cyst
items.exp: ARPKD flowchart: defect of the fibrocystin-polyductin complex affects the cilia/centrosome complex, which is seen in the collecting duct (leading to medullary cyst) and biliary duct (leading to congenital hepatic fibrosis/Caroli's syndrome/biliary ectasia). (Book p789)

items.q: A neonate with ARPKD has hepatosplenomegaly and portal hypertension. The underlying lesion is:
opts: Congenital hepatic fibrosis with biliary ectasia from biliary duct involvement
Hepatic vein thrombosis from a hypercoagulable state in the neonatal period
Viral hepatitis acquired in utero and progressing to neonatal cirrhosis
Glycogen storage disease with massive hepatic glycogen deposition
items.exp: ARPKD: the biliary duct branch of the fibrocystin defect gives congenital hepatic fibrosis (Caroli's syndrome/biliary ectasia), which produces portal hypertension. (Book p789)

items.q: What percentage of ARPKD babies with pulmonary hypoplasia die within 1 year?
items.exp: Complications of ARPKD: pulmonary hypoplasia → 70% die within 1 year (major cause of death at birth). (Book p789)

items.q: Pulmonary hypoplasia is the major cause of death at birth in ARPKD.
opts: False — portal hypertension is the commonest cause of neonatal death
False — ESRD causes 70% of neonatal deaths
items.exp: ARPKD: pulmonary hypoplasia causes 70% of deaths within 1 year and is the major cause of death at birth. (Book p789)

items.q: Match the ARPKD complication with the age of death and its cause — 1) Pulmonary hypoplasia  2) Portal hypertension (Caroli syndrome)  3) ESRD … A) Very rare; renal failure  B) 30% die at adolescence  C) 70% die within 1 year
items.exp: ARPKD complications: pulmonary hypoplasia — 70% die within 1 year (major cause of death at birth); portal hypertension from Caroli syndrome — remaining 30% die at adolescence; ESRD is very rare but causes renal failure. (Book p789)

items.q: All but one of the following are complications listed for ARPKD. Which is the odd one out?
items.exp: ARPKD complications listed are pulmonary hypoplasia, portal hypertension (Caroli syndrome) and rarely ESRD; cyst infection is an ADPKD complication. (Book p789)
